verses.text: In those days the number of followers was growing fast. The Greek-speaking Jews began to complain about the Hebrew-speaking Jews, because their widows were being left out when food was handed out each day.
So the twelve apostles called all the followers together and said, "It would not be right for us to stop preaching God's word in order to serve food at tables.
So, brothers, choose seven men from among you who are well respected and full of the Spirit and wisdom. We will put them in charge of this work.
Then we can keep giving our time to prayer and to teaching the word."

Everyone liked this idea. They chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit. They also chose Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolaus from Antioch, who had turned to the Jewish faith.
They brought these men to the apostles, who prayed and laid their hands on them.
So God's word kept spreading. The number of followers in Jerusalem grew very large, and many priests also came to believe.
Stephen was full of God's grace and power, and he did great wonders and signs among the people.
But some men began to argue with Stephen. They were from the synagogue called the Synagogue of the Freedmen, and some were from Cyrene, Alexandria, Cilicia, and Asia.
But they could not stand up against the wisdom the Spirit gave him when he spoke.
So they secretly talked some men into saying, "We heard Stephen speak evil words against Moses and against God."
They stirred up the people, the elders, and the teachers of the law. They grabbed Stephen and brought him before the council.
They brought in false witnesses, who said, "This man never stops speaking against this holy place and against the law.
We heard him say that this Jesus of Nazareth will destroy this place and change the customs Moses gave us."
Everyone sitting in the council stared at Stephen, and they saw that his face looked like the face of an angel.
